Before I spec anything — "make it pop" and "gradient hero" aren't a plan, they're the default every landing page reaches for. Whether that's actually right depends on stuff I don't have yet:

- What's this page for? Is it competing for attention / a launch moment / something meant to get screenshotted — or is it a fairly ordinary page that just needs to read clean? Those get different answers, and neither is the "safe" choice by default.
- What's the existing design system here — tokens, colors, type scale, component patterns? A gradient hero grounded in your actual palette and contrast ratios is a real design decision. A gradient hero because it's the median of every landing page a model's seen is slop with better lighting.
- Contrast: whatever gradient goes in, hero text over it needs to hit 4.5:1 (body) / 3:1 (large text/controls). That's not optional, it's the floor.

Also worth flagging: I can't generate or post a rendered mockup — no live preview, no image output. What I can do is write you a concrete spec (exact tokens, contrast targets, layout, what "pop" means in specifics) that Riley builds from.

So: tell me what this page needs to do and point me at the actual tokens/patterns in play, and I'll spec something real instead of guessing.
